thread.title: Doctors Without Borders Closes Emergency Center in Port-au-Prince
thread.title_full: Doctors Without Borders Closes Emergency Center in Port-au-Prince

author: Associated Press
title: Doctors Without Borders Closes Emergency Center in Port-au-Prince
text:
• Doctors Without Borders announced the permanent closure of its emergency care center in Port-au-Prince, Haiti.
• The closure is due to ongoing violence and gang activity in the capital.
• Over 60% of health facilities in Port-au-Prince are currently non-functioning or closed.
• The emergency center in Turgeau was targeted by armed men who opened fire on evacuation vehicles.
• Some staff members sustained minor injuries during the attack.
• The center had previously been hit by stray bullets due to its proximity to combat zones.
• Jean-Marc Biquet, head of mission for MSF in Haiti, stated that resuming activities would be too dangerous.
• Between February 24 and March 2, the center treated over 300 patients.
• In February, the center reported more than 2,500 medical consultations.
• The emergency center originally opened in Martissant in 2006 and moved to Turgeau in 2021 for security reasons.
• From 2021 to March 2025, the Turgeau center treated over 100,000 patients.
• From January to June, more than 3,100 people were reported killed in Haiti, with an additional 1,100 injured, according to the United Nations.
• Gang violence has displaced a record 1.4 million people, a 36% increase since the end of 2024.
• Almost two-thirds of new displacements occurred outside Port-au-Prince, particularly in Haiti's central region.
• The number of makeshift shelters increased from 142 in December to 238 in 2023, according to the IOM.
